title: Applewood Baby Back Ribs with Orange-Mustard Gravy
description: Lean baby back ribs braise until the meat lifts free of the bone and folds into orange-mustard gravy.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: lean pork baby back ribs
ingredients.note: Bone-in weight; choose a lean center section and remove surface fat, membrane and any thick fatty cap.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: smooth sweet orange marmalade
ingredients.note: Pass through a sieve to remove strips of peel.

ingredients.name: smooth Löwensenf Bavarian mustard
ingredients.note: Pass through a fine sieve if visibly grainy.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 300°F with apple pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {coriander} and {pepper} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Portion the rack
steps.text: Separate {ribs} into two-rib sections so the lean meat sits deep in the braising liquid.

steps.title: Cover the ribs
steps.text: Lay the ribs meat-side down in the liquid and cover the pot tightly from the outset. There is no stall-wrap temperature.

steps.title: Braise until loose
steps.text: Braise at 300°F for 1 1/2–2 1/4 hours, adding {topup} as needed to keep the liquid halfway up the ribs. Begin checking the meaty spaces near 190°F and finish when a skewer slides in and the bones pull free easily.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered ribs off heat for 8 minutes.

steps.title: Remove all bones
steps.text: Slip the meat into a covered bowl with a spoonful of braising liquid. Feel through for cartilage, bone tips and fat, then chop the lean meat coarsely.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 3/4 cup into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Build the citrus gravy
steps.text: Warm {orange} and {mustard} in the measured broth, stirring until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Serve off the bone
steps.text: Fold the pork through the gravy and divide the sauced meat between two bowls.

notes: Make ahead: Debone the ribs while warm and chill the meat in gravy. Option A uses marmalade and mustard. For gentler Option B, replace the marmalade with smooth apple butter and omit the mustard. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth.
